card.name: Talchum
card.tagline: Korean masked dance-drama of satirical folk theatre
card.profile: Talchum is a Korean masked dance-drama that encompasses dance, music and theatre, in which an ensemble of six to ten musicians accompanies masked performers who humorously explore social issues through dramatic combinations of songs, dances, movements and dialogue (UNESCO). Caricatured everyday characters - apostate monks, decadent yangban nobles, shamans - convey criticism of social hierarchy and an appeal to equality. It requires no formal stage, and the audience contributes with cheers and jeers. Regional forms include Bongsan Talchum and Hahoe byeolsingut talnori.
card.insight: 'Talchum, mask dance drama in the Republic of Korea' was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List in 2022 - Korea's 22nd ICH element - with exactly thirteen regional mask-dance-drama types collectively inscribed; its focus on social criticism fuelled a large-scale revival among university students in the 1970s and 1980s (UNESCO; Google Arts & Culture/ICHCAP).
